headline: Indiana buys basketball like a statewide religion on a Midwest budget: value-conscious, tied to the calendar of March gyms, May racing and Fever summers, and happiest paying for something that feels earned and local.
summary: Indianapolis is a mid-income, price-aware market with a flat 7% state sales tax and no tax-free weekend, so promotions and bundles do the work that tax holidays do elsewhere. Fandom is spread across the Pacers, the Fever, Purdue and Indiana, and the high school gym, which means the same household often buys several teams' gear and the Pacers share wallet with them. Spend peaks around the Pacers' playoff runs, Black Friday through Christmas, the March high school tournament and early-August back-to-school. A healthy Haliburton, the Dec 11 NBA Cup final at Hinkle and a Moments Mixtape City Edition return give a clear winter window. Cold, wet Octobers to March make layering and outerwear the real volume story.

insights.title: No tax holiday, so promotions set the calendar
insights.detail: Indiana has a flat 7% state sales tax on clothing and no back-to-school tax-free weekend, so shoppers key off retailer promotions, early-August school starts (many districts open in late July or the first week of August) and Black Friday.
insights.implication: Time kids and teen drops and footwear promotions to the last two weeks of July rather than waiting for September, and lead with bundles instead of tax-holiday messaging.

insights.title: One household, many teams
insights.detail: Pacers, Fever, Colts, Purdue, Indiana and the local high school all compete for the same wallet, and Indiana fans routinely wear college and high school gear to NBA games.
insights.implication: Price Pacers product to sit comfortably alongside a college hoodie, and use shared-state motifs such as the Indiana outline and the gym itself, not just team marks, so product works across fandoms.

insights.title: Fever demand is a second engine
insights.detail: The Indiana Fever's Caitlin Clark era made Indianapolis one of the strongest women's basketball merchandise markets, with a summer sales peak that fills the Pacers' off-season.
insights.implication: Plan women's and youth basketball product and a shared Indy basketball story for May to September so the retail rhythm runs year-round; confirm Fever licensing is separate from the Pacers.

insights.title: Cold-weather layering drives volume
insights.detail: Winters are gray, cold and often snowy, with a shoulder season that runs from October into April, so fleeces, hoodies, warm-ups and beanies outsell tees for most of the NBA season.
insights.implication: Lead with warm-ups, quarter-zips, crewnecks and outerwear in the Pacers navy, gold and gray; keep shorts and tees for May to August.

insights.title: Channel mix is team store, big-box and online first
insights.detail: Fans buy at the arena team store on game night, at mall and big-box retail (Fashion Mall at Keystone, Castleton Square, Circle Centre), at Fanatics and Nike online, and through resale; line culture and raffles are thin compared with coastal cities.
insights.implication: Make arena-night availability and a strong online release the core; treat limited drops as an event layered on Moments Mixtape rather than the base plan.

insights.title: Jersey buying is generational and value-led
insights.detail: Reggie Miller's number 31 is the heritage jersey for adults, while kids and teens skew to Haliburton, and most purchases are replica or swingman, with a lot of price-led knockoff and resale buying.
insights.implication: Prioritize youth sizes and a clear step-down tier below Swingman; use Reggie heritage product as a gifting and nostalgia play, and Haliburton as the volume name.

insights.title: Indy is a visitor retail city
insights.detail: Gen Con in the summer, the Indy 500 in May, NCAA and conference events and the Hinkle NBA Cup final on Dec 11 bring out-of-town shoppers downtown and to the arena.
insights.implication: Stock Indy-only graphics (Hinkle, Indy skyline, 500 checkered cues) in downtown retail and the team store, and keep the Cup final in mind for a limited-run tie-in.

watchouts: Butler, Purdue, Indiana and the IHSAA marks need separate licensing; do not blur college and Pacers marks.
Indianapolis Motor Speedway and Indy 500 imagery is licensed; do not use checkered or 500 marks without clearance.
Keep Fever and Pacers product distinct and do not assume one fanbase transfers to the other.
Avoid hillbilly or rural stereotyping when using small-town gym imagery; credit and partner with real communities.

extra.priceProfile: Mid-income, value-oriented market with a wide spread between affluent north-side suburbs (Carmel, Fishers, Zionsville) and lower-income urban neighborhoods and small towns. A flat 7% state sales tax with no tax holiday keeps shoppers promotion-sensitive; tier product with a strong entry price, solid mid-tier and a limited premium layer.
extra.jerseyBehavior: Replicas and Swingman dominate over authentic, with kids' sizes and gifting driving the base, Reggie Miller 31 as the heritage staple, Haliburton as the youth and volume name, and a noticeable knockoff and resale segment; tees and hoodies outsell jerseys in volume.
